description: A graduate course on systems where computation, networks and physical processes are tightly coupled: hybrid models, real-time scheduling, sensing and control networks, safety, formal verification, security and edge-to-cloud deployment. Students model plants, schedule tasks, verify controllers, attack and defend sensor networks, and deploy a small monitored system from edge device to cloud.
modelledOn: Lee and Seshia, Introduction to Embedded Systems: A Cyber-Physical Systems Approach
IEC 61508, Functional Safety of Electrical, Electronic and Programmable Electronic Safety-Related Systems
outcomes: Model a cyber-physical system as a hybrid automaton with continuous dynamics, modes, guards and resets, and simulate it.
Analyse a task set for schedulability using utilisation tests and response-time analysis, and handle shared resources and priority inversion.
Design sensing, estimation and networked actuation chains that tolerate noise, delay and packet loss.
Conduct hazard analysis and build redundant, fail-safe designs with quantified reliability.
Specify controller requirements in temporal logic, check them by model checking, reachability or falsification, and interpret counterexamples.
Threat-model a connected device and deploy a monitored edge-to-cloud pipeline with secure updates and tested failure modes.

units.title: Modelling hybrid systems
topics: CPS architecture and examples: smart grid, vehicles, medical devices and precision farming
Continuous dynamics: state-space models, linearisation, zero-order-hold discretisation and numerical simulation
Discrete dynamics: finite state machines and timed automata
Hybrid automata: modes, guards and resets; Zeno behaviour; the thermostat and bouncing ball
Co-simulation and model-based design: fidelity versus cost

units.title: Real-time scheduling and timing analysis
topics: Tasks, periods, deadlines and jitter; hard versus soft real-time
Fixed-priority scheduling: rate-monotonic priorities, the utilisation bound and response-time analysis
Earliest-deadline-first scheduling and exact schedulability tests
Shared resources: priority inversion, priority inheritance and priority ceiling protocols
Worst-case execution time: measurement versus static analysis, caches and pipelines
Control-scheduling co-design: effect of sampling jitter and delay on stability

units.title: Sensing, networking and actuation
topics: Sensor models, noise and calibration; complementary and weighted fusion
State estimation: the Kalman filter and its extended form
Control and industrial buses: CAN arbitration and message response times, Modbus
Low-power wireless links (LoRa, BLE, Zigbee), duty cycles and MQTT publish-subscribe
Time synchronisation: clock drift, NTP, PTP and time-triggered architectures
Actuator limits and networked control with delay and packet loss

units.title: Safety and fault tolerance
topics: Hazard analysis: HAZOP, FMEA and fault trees
Safety standards, integrity levels and safety cases
Redundancy: dual and triple modular redundancy, voting and watchdog timers
Fault models (crash, transient, Byzantine); detection, isolation and recovery
Reliability metrics: failure rate, MTBF, availability and Markov models
Graceful degradation and fail-safe design

units.title: Formal verification of controllers
topics: Requirement specification: LTL, CTL and signal temporal logic
Model checking: state-space exploration, safety and liveness, counterexamples
Reachability analysis for hybrid systems; invariants and barrier certificates
Lyapunov functions and stability certificates for controllers
Falsification and runtime monitoring of CPS using search and robustness measures
Assume-guarantee contracts and compositional verification

units.title: Security of connected devices
topics: CPS threat models: spoofing, replay and false data injection on sensors and actuators
Secure boot, signed firmware updates and hardware roots of trust
Securing device protocols: TLS and MQTT authentication under key-management limits
Case studies in power-grid and industrial control incidents; physics-based anomaly detection

units.title: Edge-to-cloud deployment
topics: Edge, fog and cloud tiers: latency budgets and placement of computation
Data pipelines: MQTT ingestion, stream processing and time-series storage
Digital twins: model synchronisation, cloud state estimation and what-if analysis
Fleet management: over-the-air updates, orchestration, cost, resilience and failure injection

units.title: Project: an end-to-end CPS
topics: Requirements and architecture for an end-to-end CPS
Verification and safety argument for the controller
Evaluation under injected faults and attacks
Technical report and demonstration

schedule.title: Hybrid systems and state-space models
schedule.exercise: Model a greenhouse heater as a state-space plant plus a thermostat state machine, discretise it, and simulate temperature for a 24 hour day.

tasks.title: Discretise a first-order thermal model with zero-order hold at two sampling periods and compare the step responses with the continuous solution
Step a timed automaton for a crossing gate in the visualiser and record the state and clock values for a train arrival trace
Simulate a linearised inverted pendulum with state feedback and report the largest sampling period for which it stays stable

schedule.title: Hybrid automata and co-simulation
schedule.exercise: Specify the bouncing ball and a thermostat as hybrid automata with guards and resets, and explain Zeno behaviour and how to detect it.

tasks.title: Simulate a bouncing ball hybrid automaton with event detection, plot height over time and detect the accumulation of bounces
Build a two-mode thermostat hybrid model, add a hysteresis band, and measure the switching frequency for three band widths
Co-simulate a plant model and a controller running at different rates and quantify the error against a single monolithic simulation

schedule.title: Real-time tasks and fixed-priority scheduling
schedule.exercise: Check whether a set of three periodic sensor tasks is schedulable under rate-monotonic and earliest-deadline-first, using utilisation and response-time analysis.

tasks.title: Run a three-task set under rate-monotonic scheduling in the visualiser and mark the first deadline miss, if any, on the timeline
Compute response times for a 4-task set by fixed-point iteration and compare the results with the utilisation bound test
Find the task set utilisation at which earliest-deadline-first still meets every deadline but rate-monotonic fails, and demonstrate it on the timeline

schedule.title: Resources, WCET and control timing
schedule.exercise: Explain how priority inversion can disrupt a flight-controller task, apply priority inheritance, and quantify the effect of timing jitter on loop stability.

tasks.title: Reproduce a priority inversion with three tasks and a shared lock, then enable priority inheritance and compare the high-priority delay
Measure the execution time of a sensor-processing routine over 1000 runs on the bench and report the mean, maximum and a safe WCET bound
Simulate a feedback loop with growing sampling jitter and find the jitter level at which the closed loop loses stability

schedule.title: Sensors, fusion and state estimation
schedule.exercise: Fuse an accelerometer and a gyroscope to estimate tilt, derive a Kalman filter for a 1D position tracker, and compute CAN message response times.

tasks.title: Read an accelerometer and a gyroscope on the bench, apply a complementary filter and compare the tilt estimate with a known angle
Implement a Kalman filter for a 1D position and velocity tracker with noisy readings and plot estimate error against the raw measurement
Simulate CAN bus arbitration among five message identifiers and compute worst-case response time of the lowest-priority message

schedule.title: Wireless links, time and networked control
schedule.exercise: Design a soil-moisture sensor network for a farm using low-power radio, compute battery life, and find how packet loss degrades remote control.

tasks.title: Publish simulated soil-moisture readings from a node over MQTT with retained messages and a last-will message, and verify subscribers receive them
Simulate two clocks with different drift rates synchronised by periodic exchange and report the maximum offset for three sync intervals
Close a control loop over a network with random delay and 5 to 30 percent packet loss, and plot the performance against loss rate

schedule.title: Hazards, standards and redundancy
schedule.exercise: Build a fault tree for loss of braking in an electric tricycle taxi, assign probabilities, and show the effect of triple redundancy on the top-event probability.

tasks.title: Draw a fault tree for a failed infusion pump alarm with at least six basic events and compute the top-event probability
Implement a watchdog timer on the microcontroller, force a program hang and show the board recovers within the timeout
Simulate triple modular redundancy with a majority voter under independent faults and compare reliability with a single channel across 5 failure rates

schedule.title: Fault models, reliability and degradation
schedule.exercise: Model the availability of a solar-powered clinic fridge monitor with a Markov chain, and design a degradation plan for a failed sensor.

tasks.title: Compute steady-state availability from a two-state Markov model for three repair rates and plot availability against repair time
Run a consensus protocol in the visualiser with one crashed node and then one Byzantine node, and record when agreement fails
Inject a stuck-at fault into a sensor on the bench, detect it by a plausibility check and switch the controller to a safe fallback mode

schedule.title: Temporal logic and model checking
schedule.exercise: Write five requirements for a traffic-light controller in temporal logic, check them by model checking, and interpret a counterexample trace.

tasks.title: Translate five plain-language requirements for a level-crossing controller into LTL formulas and check each on three given traces
Explore the state space of a given controller model, find the state violating a safety property and read the counterexample path
Compute the reachable set of a 2D linear system from an initial box for 20 steps and decide whether it reaches an unsafe region

schedule.title: Stability certificates, falsification and contracts
schedule.exercise: Prove stability of a closed-loop system with a Lyapunov function, falsify a cruise controller specification by search, and write an assume-guarantee contract.

tasks.title: Verify a candidate quadratic Lyapunov function for a 2-state system by checking its derivative is negative on a grid
Search for input signals that violate a cruise controller specification using random sampling and report the robustness of the best trace
Write assume-guarantee contracts for a sensor and a controller and check by simulation that composing them meets the system requirement

schedule.title: Securing connected devices
schedule.exercise: Threat-model a smart meter, show a replay attack on its readings, and add defences: nonces, signed firmware and an anomaly detector based on physics.

tasks.title: Capture and replay a meter reading message in a simulated network and then block replay with a sequence number check
Configure an MQTT broker with authentication and topic access control, and verify that an unauthorised client cannot publish a command
Build a residual-based anomaly detector for a water tank level using a physics model, and measure detection delay for an injected false reading

schedule.title: Edge, fog and cloud deployment
schedule.exercise: Deploy sensor ingestion, a time-series store and an alert rule in the cloud, place control at the edge and test what happens when the uplink fails.

tasks.title: Create a queue, a function and a time-series bucket to ingest simulated sensor messages and verify 1000 messages are stored
Place a control loop at the edge and analytics in the cloud, measure the latency of each path and check it against a 50 ms budget
Inject a regional outage and a slow network into the console, observe the pipeline, and add retry and local buffering to avoid data loss

schedule.title: Project: build and evaluate an end-to-end CPS
schedule.exercise: Demonstrate your CPS, present its requirements, model, safety argument and verification results, and report its behaviour under injected faults and attacks.

tasks.title: Draw the architecture of your CPS with sensors, controller, network, edge and cloud, and annotate latency and failure assumptions on each link
Verify two safety requirements of your controller by reachability or simulation sweeps and report the margin to the unsafe set
Run your system on the bench with a sensor fault, a delayed message and a spoofed command, and record how it behaves in each case
